items.description: There are a lot of tools out there (see the tools section below), but some tools are particularly great for early experimentation. These tools can be used right in your web browser, so you can get started without installing software locally.
items.title: Experiment with Tools

items.description: These tools run entirely in your web browser, so no data is sent anywhere.

items.title: Demystify Lite
items.description: This runs Siegfried WASM on your files in your browser and outputs a Demystify formatted report profiling your collection and highlighting files that might require specific attention during appraisal, such as duplicates; and through various preservation activities, such as caring for file names encoded using specific character-encodings.

items.title: warc-analyser
items.description: Proof-of-concept that analyses WARC files in your browser. See https://github.com/edsu/warc-analyzer for more information.

items.title: In-Browser Tools
"Small"
items.description: Collection of "the smallest possible syntactically valid files in different programming/scripting/markup languages."

items.title: digicam corpus
items.description: Contains a corpus of Digital Camera files collected by Tyler Thorsted.

items.title: Archivematica Sample Data
items.description: Includes OPF format corpus, as well as other test material.

items.title: The Skeleton Test Suite
items.description: Builds test files from PRONOM binary and container signatures. These can be used to test DROID and other (compatible) identification tools.

items.title: PREFORMA Ground Truth Classes
items.description: Instructions how to reproduce validation-failing files for Matroska, FFV1, LPCM, TIFF, and PDF formats.

items.title: RDSS Archivematica Test Data Corpus
items.description: A collection of research dataset files used for testing Archivematica integration and functionality in the JISC Research Data Shared Service (RDSS).

items.title: MediaArea-RegressionTestingFiles
items.description: Public regression testing files for MediaArea. Contains AVI, FLV, MPEG Audio, MOV, MPEG-4, MPEG-PS, and Matroska files.

items.title: See also: The PDF Association's list of PDF-focused corpora
veraPDF Corpus
items.description: For PDF/A.

items.title: PDF Differences
items.description: Targeted test files that highlight specific portability and interoperability issues by the PDF Association.

items.title: KBNLresearch/epubPolicyTests
items.description: Some #epub samples with encryption, DTBook content and foreign resources, with corresponding #epubcheck output.

items.title: openjpeg-data
items.description: Test files for OpenJPEG.

items.title: jpylyzer-test-files
items.description: Test files for Jpylyzer.

If the existing corpora aren't cutting it, perhaps you can contribute to the OPF Format Corpus hosted on GitHub. There's a guide here on how to contribute (archived version) or you can contact OPF for help on how to get involved.
items.title: Building Corpora

items.description: Web archives can provide a useful source of files of particular formats. For example, search via the UKWA interface. Note that UKWA is offline at present.
items.title: Sourcing test files from web archives

items.description: Tyler Thorsted's File Formats - Finding Samples repository lists various resources that can be used to find file format samples.
items.title: Sourcing test files

items.description: Contributing to the development and improvement of tools is easy, even if you're not technical. Check out this guide to making small documentation edits, or raising issues on GitHub
items.title: Improve The Tools
